title: US General Milley estimates Russian military casualties above 100,000
body:
On 9 November 2022, US Army General Mark Milley, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said at the Economic Club of New York that well over 100,000 Russian soldiers had been killed or wounded in the war, now in its ninth month. The Associated Press reported the remarks on 10 November 2022. Milley said the Ukrainian side was probably experiencing similar losses and that as many as 40,000 Ukrainian civilians had been killed or wounded.

The figures were presented as estimates, using terms such as well over and as many as, and the report did not give sources or methodology. Reuters noted that the number was the highest US estimate of casualties up to that point.

Milley spoke as Russia announced a retreat from Kherson. He said Russia had 20,000 to 30,000 troops there and that a full withdrawal could take several weeks, and that its intent was uncertain, since Russia might be preserving forces for defensive lines south of the Dnipro or resetting for a spring offensive. President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that the pullout could be a feint. Milley also said there might be a window for negotiations, but that both sides would first need to accept that military victory might not be achievable.
